cards.text: Solomon, son of David and king of Israel, is still handing out proverbs (Prov 1:1; 10:1). Most of these short sayings are two lines going head to head, one way to live against the other. He starts in the marketplace, where every sale gets weighed on a scale.

cards.question: A seller rigs his scale so every customer gets a little less than they paid for. How does the LORD see that dishonest scale?

answers.text: As a small thing He overlooks

cards.question: Now flip it. A seller's weight is accurate, right down to the last crumb. Solomon says that accurate weight is the LORD's ___.

cards.text: Next up, pride struts in like it owns the bakery, and Solomon says it never walks in alone. Friend, I wear a hat THIS tall, so I'm taking notes.

cards.question: When pride comes in, what does Solomon say follows right behind it?
True or false: Solomon says that with humility comes wisdom.

cards.text: Then Solomon lines up two kinds of people: the upright and the faithless. Same road, VERY different trips.

cards.question: What does Solomon say guides the upright?
And the faithless on that same road? What does Solomon say destroys them?

cards.text: Then Solomon puts money on the scale and says riches are worthless in the day of wrath. Friend, Mother Miller bought me for 25 cents, so I've been telling people money isn't everything for YEARS.

cards.question: Riches can't help in the day of wrath. Solomon says ___ is what brings deliverance from death.

cards.text: Solomon keeps walking that road. The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the wicked fall because someone else trips them up.
The righteousness of the upright delivers them. But the faithless? Solomon says they're trapped by their own ___.

cards.text: Now Solomon looks at the end of the road. When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the righteous man and the wicked man both get delivered from trouble.

cards.text: Next, Solomon talks about the mouth. The ungodly man can destroy his neighbor with nothing but his mouth, and friend, one group chat can do EXACTLY that before lunch.

cards.question: Solomon puts the righteous on the other side of that line. What does he say they're rescued through?

cards.text: Now Solomon zooms out to a whole city. When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.

cards.question: The mouth of the wicked can tear a city down. So what does Solomon say builds a city up?

cards.text: Then Solomon gets up close and personal. Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says a man of understanding remains silent.

cards.text: Then the gossip leans in: "Okay. I am NOT supposed to say anything... BUT." Solomon says a gossip reveals a secret.

cards.question: A gossip reveals a secret, but Solomon says a trustworthy person keeps a ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon goes big again. He says a whole nation falls for lack of guidance.

cards.question: If a nation falls for lack of guidance, what does Solomon say brings deliverance?

cards.text: Then some money advice: he who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer. Friend, I shared a drawer with an expired coupon that still believed in itself, and even HE wouldn't cosign for a stranger.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the one who hates indebtedness is secure.

cards.text: Next, Solomon puts a gracious woman and ruthless men side by side. They both walk away with something, but it is NOT the same something.

cards.question: Ruthless men gain only wealth. But Solomon says a gracious woman attains ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon talks about kindness and cruelty. You'd think kindness is all about the other person, but watch who Solomon says comes out ahead.

cards.question: A cruel man brings trouble on himself. Who does Solomon say a kind man benefits?

cards.text: The wicked man works and works and earns an empty wage. That's opening your paycheck and finding a really nice DRAWING of a paycheck.

cards.question: The wicked man's wage is empty. But Solomon says he who ___ righteousness reaps a true reward.
True or false: Solomon says the pursuit of evil leads to life in the end.

cards.text: Remember those dishonest scales? Now Solomon says the perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD too.

cards.question: On the other side, who does Solomon say are the LORD's delight?

cards.text: Solomon starts the home stretch with a promise. Be assured, he says, the wicked will not go unpunished.

cards.question: The wicked won't go unpunished. What does Solomon say about the offspring of the righteous?

cards.text: Then Solomon paints a picture: a gold ring in a pig's snout, and he says that's what a beautiful woman who lacks discretion is like. Picture it, friend. Fine polished gold, going nose-first into the mud.

cards.question: What's the point of Solomon's gold ring in a pig's snout?

answers.text: Beauty without discretion is out of place
Gold rings are a sign of pride
Beauty matters more than good judgment

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the desire of the righteous leads only to good.

cards.text: Now Solomon flips the math upside down: one man gives freely and ends up gaining even MORE. I'm a stamper, not a mathematician, but I've been staring at that one for a WHILE.

cards.question: Another man withholds what is right. Where does Solomon say that leaves him?

cards.text: Then Solomon stays on giving. A generous soul will prosper.

cards.question: A generous soul will prosper. And Solomon says he who refreshes others will himself be ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon heads to the grain market. One man is hoarding grain, and another is selling it.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the people will bless the hoarder of grain.

cards.text: Then Solomon says it plain: he who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it. Go looking for trouble, friend, and trouble RSVPs.

cards.question: Next, Solomon talks about a man who trusts in his riches. What does he say happens to him?
True or false: Solomon says the righteous will fall right along with the man who trusts in his riches.

cards.text: Then a warning about home: he who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind. You wait all that time for your inheritance, and it's... a breeze.

cards.question: Where does Solomon say the fool ends up?

answers.text: Servant to the wise of heart

cards.question: Solomon says the fruit of the righteous is a ___ of life, and he who wins souls is wise.

cards.text: And Solomon closes the chapter with one last line: "If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!" That's a LOT to weigh, friend.

findings.problem: The question opens with "And the faithless on that same road?" The phrase "that same road" points back to card 7's "Same road" line, which is no longer on screen. The question also never says who is on the other side of the contrast.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "The ungodly man can destroy his neighbor with nothing but his mouth" stretches Proverbs 11:9. The verse says "With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor" and nothing more. "Nothing but" adds an exclusivity the text doesn't have, and this is the fact line, not the joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Solomon puts the righteous on the other side of that line" points back to the previous story card, which is no longer on screen. The question never says what the line is: the ungodly man destroying his neighbor with his mouth.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 13's setup says "You'd think kindness is all about the other person, but watch who Solomon says comes out ahead." That rules out both wrong answers, "His master" and "The king," because both are other people. The question's own opening, "A cruel man brings trouble on himself," points straight to "Himself" as well.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "The wicked man works and works and earns an empty wage" adds repeated labor that Proverbs 11:18 doesn't state. The verse only says he "earns an empty wage." The exaggeration sits in the fact line, not in the joke that follows it.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "On the other side, who does Solomon say are the LORD's delight?" points back to card 18 with "the other side," but card 18 is no longer on screen. The question never says what the other side is: the perverse in heart being an abomination to the LORD.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Several story cards just restate the verse, often behind the same "Then Solomon..." opener, with no Papa Dorin voice. These are stop 1 cards 12 and 15, stop 2 cards 1, 3 and 7, and stop 3 cards 1, 8 and 10. For example, stop 3 card 8 reads only "Then Solomon stays on giving. A generous soul will prosper."

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
